chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The performer of Tamattu', when he looks at the houses of Makkah, cuts off the Talbiyya.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The ritual recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' during Hajj
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.بُيُوتِ مَكَّةَ: The houses of Makkah, referring to the visible structures of the city

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' stop reciting the Talbiyya?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the precise moment the Mu'tamatti' transitions from the state of Ihram for Hajj to that of Umrah by ceasing the Talbiyya upon sighting the houses of Makkah. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of the Tamattu' pilgrim, who performs Umrah first and remains in a non-Ihram state until the days of Hajj, distinguishing it from the Qiran and Ifrad methods. The cessation of Talbiyya signifies the completion of the Umrah rites and the readiness for the subsequent Hajj obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The performer of Tumatto, when he looks at the houses of Makkah, should cut off the Talbiyya’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) on seeing the houses of Makkah must stop saying al-Talbiyah (here I am, O Lord, to obey Your command).”’
